source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν σαββάτῳ διαπορεύεσθαι αὐτὸν διὰ σπορίμων, καὶ ἔτιλλον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤσθιον τοὺς στάχυας ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν.

records.literal_gloss: It came about then on a Sabbath [that] to be passing through him through grainfields, and were plucking the disciples of him and were eating the heads of grain, rubbing [them] in the hands.

en.L: Now it happened on a Sabbath [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was passing through grainfields, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were plucking and eating the heads of grain, rubbing [them] in [their] hands.
en.B: On a Sabbath Jesus was walking through fields of grain. His disciples were pulling off heads of grain, rubbing them between their hands, and eating them.
en.R: One Sabbath day Jesus was walking through some fields of grain. His disciples picked some heads of grain. They rubbed them in their hands to get the seeds out, and they ate them.

fr.L: Or il arriva, un jour de sabbat, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} traversait des champs de blé, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples arrachaient et mangeaient les épis, en [les] frottant dans [leurs] mains.
fr.B: Un jour de sabbat, Jésus passait à travers des champs de blé. Ses disciples arrachaient des épis, les froissaient entre leurs mains et en mangeaient les grains.
fr.R: Un jour de sabbat, Jésus marchait à travers des champs de blé. Ses disciples ont cueilli des épis. Ils les ont frottés dans leurs mains pour en faire sortir les grains, et ils les ont mangés.

decisions.choice: on a Sabbath: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: on the second-first Sabbath, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, including most later ones, read "on the second-first Sabbath", using a word found nowhere else in Greek writing. Its meaning is unknown: perhaps the second Sabbath of a series, or the first Sabbath after Passover. Several early manuscripts lack the word, and it may have begun as a note in the margin. The meaning of the verse is the same either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Sabbath: the seventh day, from sunset on Friday to sunset on Saturday, set apart by God's law as a day of rest
decisions.reason: The commandment forbids work on the seventh day (Exodus 20:8-11), even at harvest time (Exodus 34:21). How to keep it was a constant question for devout Jews.

decisions.choice: plucking and rubbing heads of grain: allowed by the law on other days
decisions.reason: The law let a passer-by pick heads of grain by hand in a neighbor's field, though not use a sickle (Deuteronomy 23:25). The question in 6:2 is about the day, not the field: picking and rubbing grain could be counted as reaping and threshing.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: to get the seeds out
decisions.reason: Readable says why they rubbed the grain: to free the kernels from the husks.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level, David's story (6:3-4) and the house-builders (6:48-49) included
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. What Jesus says keeps the tenses of speech, so the story of David he retells is in the passé composé. Literal renders Luke's "it came about that" as "il arriva que". This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: un jour de sabbat, le sabbat (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form for the New Testament: "sabbat" is a common noun in French and takes no capital. "Samedi" would lose the day's religious meaning (m2).

source.text: τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων εἶπαν· Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν;

records.literal_gloss: Some then of the Pharisees said, Why are you doing what not is lawful on the Sabbaths?

en.L: But some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?"
en.B: Some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing something the law forbids on the Sabbath?"
en.R: Some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing something that the law does not allow on the Sabbath day?"

fr.L: Mais quelques-uns des Pharisiens dirent : « Pourquoi faites-vous ce qui n’est pas permis le jour du sabbat ? »
fr.B: Quelques Pharisiens dirent : « Pourquoi faites-vous, le jour du sabbat, ce que la Loi interdit ? »
fr.R: Quelques Pharisiens ont dit : « Pourquoi faites-vous une chose que la Loi ne permet pas le jour du sabbat ? »

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement of Jews devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were respected teachers who kept the law strictly, together with the traditions handed down about how to keep it (Mark 7:3). Paul had been one (Philippians 3:5). They often watched and questioned Jesus (5:17, 21, 30).

decisions.choice: you: plural, spoken to the disciples
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. In Luke they question the disciples, and Jesus answers for them (6:3).

decisions.choice: what is not lawful: work forbidden on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Picking and rubbing grain counted as reaping and threshing, which the law forbade on the Sabbath (Exodus 34:21). Later Jewish teaching lists reaping and threshing among the main kinds of forbidden work.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbaths: a plural form meaning the Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The plural is often used for a single Sabbath (4:31; 13:10).

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens, capitalised; "vous" (plural) to the disciples; la Loi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet capitalises the names of Jewish groups, as in John and Mark. The Greek verb is plural (m2), so French says "vous". Balanced and Readable name the Law of Moses as "la Loi", with a capital, as the term sheet does.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὁπότε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες;

records.literal_gloss: And answering to them said Jesus, Not even this have you read, what did David when was hungry he and those with him being,

en.L: And answering them, Jesus said, "Have you not even read this, what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him,
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Have you not even read about what David did when he and the men with him were hungry?
en.R: Jesus answered them, "Have you not read in the Scriptures what David did? He and his men were hungry.

fr.L: Et, leur répondant, Jésus dit : « N’avez-vous même pas lu ce qu’a fait David lorsqu’il a eu faim, lui et ceux qui étaient avec lui,
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « N’avez-vous donc pas lu ce qu’a fait David quand lui et ses compagnons ont eu faim ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Vous n’avez pas lu dans les Écritures ce qu’a fait David ? Lui et ses hommes avaient faim.

decisions.choice: what David did: 1 Samuel 21:1-6
decisions.reason: Fleeing from Saul, David came to the priest Ahimelech at Nob and asked for food. The only bread there was the holy bread that had been taken from the LORD's table, and the priest gave it to David for himself and his men.

decisions.choice: have you not even read this: a question that expects the answer yes
alternatives: a real question about what they had read
decisions.reason: The words "not even" make the question sharp: men who study the Scriptures have surely read this story, yet they have missed its point.

decisions.choice: in the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Readable says where they would have read it.

decisions.choice: two sentences: the question, then David's hunger
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the question short and tells the story in the following sentences.

source.text: ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: how he entered into the house of the God and the loaves of the presentation having taken ate and gave to those with him, which not it is lawful to eat except only the priests?

en.L: how he entered into the house of God, and taking the loaves of the presentation, he ate and gave [some] to those with him, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?"
en.B: He went into the house of God, took the bread set out before God, and ate it, and he gave some to the men with him. Yet the law allows no one but the priests to eat that bread."
en.R: David went into the house of God and took the special bread that was placed there before God. He ate it, and he gave some to his men. But the law said that only the priests could eat that bread."

fr.L: comment il est entré dans la maison de Dieu et, ayant pris les pains de la présentation, en a mangé et en a donné à ceux [qui étaient] avec lui, [des pains] qu’il n’est permis de manger qu’aux seuls prêtres ? »
fr.B: Il est entré dans la maison de Dieu, il a pris les pains déposés devant Dieu, il en a mangé et il en a donné aux hommes qui l’accompagnaient. Pourtant la Loi ne permet à personne d’en manger, sauf aux prêtres. »
fr.R: David est entré dans la maison de Dieu. Il a pris le pain spécial qu’on avait placé là, devant Dieu. Il en a mangé, et il en a donné à ses hommes. Pourtant, la Loi disait que seuls les prêtres pouvaient manger ce pain. »

decisions.choice: the house of God: the tent of worship, then standing at Nob
decisions.reason: The temple had not yet been built in David's day. The tent of worship, the tabernacle, was then at Nob (1 Samuel 21:1).

decisions.choice: the loaves of the presentation: the twelve loaves set out before the LORD
decisions.reason: Every Sabbath twelve fresh loaves were set in two rows on the table in the holy place, before the LORD. The old loaves were holy and were to be eaten only by the priests, in a holy place (Leviticus 24:5-9; Exodus 25:30).

decisions.choice: which it is not lawful to eat: Scripture tells of David's act without condemning it
decisions.reason: The argument runs from the greater case: if David and his men were not condemned for eating the holy bread when they were hungry, the disciples of the one greater than David are not condemned for picking grain. 6:5 states the claim behind it.

decisions.choice: a statement, not the end of the question
decisions.reason: The Greek question runs on from 6:3. Balanced and Readable tell the story as statements, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: the bread set out before God (B); the special bread that was placed there before God (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means bread set out in God's presence. Balanced and Readable say so in plain words.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Κύριός ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Lord is of the Sabbath the Son of the Man.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "[The] Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "The Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath."
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath day."

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait : « Le Fils de l’homme est Seigneur du sabbat. »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Le Fils de l’homme est le Seigneur du sabbat. »
fr.R: Puis Jésus leur a dit : « Le Fils de l’homme est Seigneur : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a autorité sur le sabbat. »

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
alternatives: a son of man: simply a human being
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "son of man" can mean a human being (Psalm 8:5). In Daniel 7:13-14 one like a son of man receives from God authority and a kingdom. Jesus uses the title of himself, as he did in 5:24.

decisions.choice: Lord of the Sabbath: the one with authority over the Sabbath
alternatives: one who simply keeps the Sabbath well
decisions.reason: God gave the Sabbath (Genesis 2:2-3; Exodus 20:8-11). To claim authority over it, to say what it is for and what is fitting on it, is a great claim. The word "Lord" stands first in the sentence for emphasis.

decisions.choice: this verse here, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse placed after 6:10, as in one ancient manuscript
decisions.reason: One ancient manuscript of the Gospels moves this saying after 6:10 and puts in its place a story, found nowhere else, about a man working on the Sabbath. Almost all manuscripts have the order of the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord over the Sabbath (B, R); Lord of the Sabbath (L)
decisions.reason: "Over" makes clear that the title means authority.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: Seigneur du sabbat (L, B); est Seigneur : il a autorité sur le sabbat (R)
decisions.reason: French "Seigneur du sabbat" already says lordship over the day, so Literal and Balanced need no "over". Readable spells out the authority (m2), as the English Readable's "over" does; the "il" is the Son of Man, Jesus, and takes the deity_pronoun setting.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν· καὶ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά·

records.literal_gloss: It came about then on another Sabbath [that] to enter him into the synagogue and to teach; and there was a man there and the hand of him the right was withered;

en.L: And it happened on another Sabbath [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered into the synagogue and was teaching. And a man was there, and his right hand was withered.
en.B: Another Sabbath came, and Jesus went into the synagogue and taught there. A man was present whose right hand was withered.
en.R: On another Sabbath day Jesus went into the synagogue and taught the people. There was a man there whose right hand was weak and shrunken. He could not use it.

fr.L: Et il arriva, un autre sabbat, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra dans la synagogue et y enseignait. Et il y avait là un homme, et sa main droite était desséchée.
fr.B: Un autre jour de sabbat, Jésus entra dans la synagogue et se mit à enseigner. Il s’y trouvait un homme dont la main droite était desséchée.
fr.R: Un autre jour de sabbat, Jésus est entré dans la synagogue et il a enseigné ceux qui étaient là. Il y avait un homme dont la main droite était paralysée et toute maigre. Il ne pouvait pas s’en servir.

decisions.choice: synagogue: the local meeting place where Jews gathered on the Sabbath for prayer and the reading and teaching of Scripture
decisions.reason: There was one temple, in Jerusalem, but a synagogue in every town. Jesus taught in them (4:15-16, 44).

decisions.choice: withered: dried up, shrunken and useless
decisions.reason: The word means dry. It describes a hand wasted or paralyzed, as in 1 Kings 13:4.

decisions.choice: his right hand: the hand used for work
decisions.reason: Only Luke says which hand it was. Losing the use of the right hand meant losing the ability to earn a living.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: He could not use it.
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a withered hand meant for the man.

source.text: παρετηροῦντο δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεύει, ἵνα εὕρωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Were watching closely then the scribes and the Pharisees whether on the Sabbath he heals, so that they might find to accuse him.

en.L: And the scribes and the Pharisees were watching closely [to see] whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find [a way] to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The scribes and the Pharisees kept a close watch on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to see whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal on the Sabbath, so that they could find a charge to bring against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The teachers of the law and the Pharisees watched Jesus carefully. They wanted to see whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal anyone on the Sabbath day. Then they would have something to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} of.

fr.L: Or les scribes et les Pharisiens observaient de près [pour voir] s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} guérirait le jour du sabbat, afin de trouver [de quoi] {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser.
fr.B: Les scribes et les Pharisiens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} surveillaient de près pour voir s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ferait une guérison le jour du sabbat ; ils voulaient trouver un motif d’accusation contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Les spécialistes de la Loi et les Pharisiens surveillaient Jésus attentivement. Ils voulaient voir s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait guérir quelqu’un le jour du sabbat. Comme cela, ils auraient une raison de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser.

decisions.choice: scribes: experts who taught and explained the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word means men of letters, but in the Gospels the scribes are teachers of the law. Many of them were Pharisees (5:21, 30).

decisions.choice: heal on the Sabbath: counted by many as work, unless a life was in danger
alternatives: clearly forbidden in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The law of Moses does not mention healing on the Sabbath. Later Jewish teaching allowed help on the Sabbath when a life was in danger, but this man's hand could have waited a day (compare 13:14).

decisions.choice: were watching closely: watching for a chance to catch him
decisions.reason: The verb means to watch carefully, often with hostile intent (14:1; 20:20).

decisions.choice: teachers of the law
decisions.reason: "Scribes" today suggests people who copy documents. Readable says what they did.

decisions.choice: [a way] (L); a charge (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only that they might find to accuse him; something to accuse him with is meant.

decisions.choice: les scribes (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
alternatives: les maîtres de la Loi at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms: Literal and Balanced keep the traditional title, and Readable says what they did, as the English Readable's "teachers of the law" does (m1).

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν, εἶπεν δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα· Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη.

records.literal_gloss: He but knew the thoughts of them, said and to the man the withered having the hand, Rise and stand into the middle; and having risen he stood.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew their thoughts, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man who had the withered hand, "Get up and stand in the middle." And rising, he stood [there].
en.B: He knew their thoughts, though, and said to the man with the withered hand, "Get up and come stand in the middle." The man rose and stood there.
en.R: But Jesus knew what was in their minds. He said to the man with the weak hand, "Get up and stand here where everyone can see you." So the man got up and stood there.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} connaissait leurs pensées, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme qui avait la main desséchée : « Lève-toi et tiens-toi au milieu. » Et, s’étant levé, il se tint [là].
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} connaissait leurs pensées, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme à la main desséchée : « Lève-toi, et viens te placer au milieu. » L’homme se leva et resta debout.
fr.R: Mais Jésus savait ce qu’ils pensaient. Il a dit à l’homme à la main malade : « Lève-toi et mets-toi ici, où tout le monde peut te voir. » Alors l’homme s’est levé et il est resté là, debout.

decisions.choice: he knew their thoughts: he knew what they were reasoning in secret
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus knowing hidden thoughts (5:22; 9:47), as Simeon said the thoughts of many hearts would be revealed (2:35).

decisions.choice: stand in the middle: where everyone in the synagogue could see
decisions.reason: Jesus does not heal in secret. He puts the question of 6:9 before them all.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear who stood up.

decisions.choice: here where everyone can see you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς, εἰ ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀπολέσαι;

records.literal_gloss: Said then Jesus to them, I ask you whether it is lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, life to save or to destroy?

en.L: Then Jesus said to them, "I ask you, is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy [it]?"
en.B: Then Jesus said to them, "Let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} put a question to you: on the Sabbath, does the law allow doing good, or doing harm? Saving a life, or destroying it?"
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "I want to ask you something. On the Sabbath day, does the law let us do good, or do harm? Does it let us save a life, or destroy it?"

fr.L: Puis Jésus leur dit : « Je vous demande : est-il permis, le jour du sabbat, de faire du bien ou de faire du mal, de sauver une vie ou de [la] détruire ? »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit alors : « J’ai une question à vous poser : le jour du sabbat, la Loi permet-elle de faire du bien, ou de faire du tort ? De sauver une vie, ou de la détruire ? »
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus leur a dit : « Je veux vous demander quelque chose. Le jour du sabbat, est-ce que la Loi nous permet de faire du bien, ou de faire du mal ? Est-ce qu’elle nous permet de sauver une vie, ou de la détruire ? »

decisions.choice: life: a person's life
decisions.reason: The word can mean the soul, but beside "save" and "destroy" it means a person's life, as often (9:24; 12:22).

decisions.choice: do good or do harm: refusing to do good when one can is itself a kind of harm
alternatives: a choice only between healing and killing
decisions.reason: Jesus does not allow a middle way. While he plans to do good, his opponents are planning harm against him on the same Sabbath (6:7, 11).

decisions.choice: do evil: do harm
decisions.reason: The verb is the opposite of "do good" and means to harm someone.

decisions.choice: doing harm (B); do harm (R)
decisions.reason: As the meaning decision explains, the contrast is between helping and harming.

decisions.choice: does the law let us
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question in plain words.

decisions.choice: faire du mal (L, R); faire du tort (B)
decisions.reason: "Faire le mal" would mean doing moral evil in general; the contrast is between helping and harming someone (m3), which French says with "faire du mal" and, in Balanced, "faire du tort".

source.text: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου· ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having looked around at all them he said to him, Stretch out the hand of you. He then did, and was restored the hand of him.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had looked around at all of them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Stretch out your hand." He did [it], and his hand was restored.
en.B: Jesus looked around at every one of them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man, "Hold out your hand." The man did, and his hand was made healthy again.
en.R: Jesus looked around at all of them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man, "Hold out your hand." The man held it out, and his hand was healed. It was normal again.

fr.L: Et, les ayant tous regardés à la ronde, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Étends ta main. » Il le fit, et sa main fut rétablie.
fr.B: Jésus les regarda tous, l’un après l’autre, puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme : « Tends la main. » L’homme le fit, et sa main redevint saine.
fr.R: Jésus les a tous regardés. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit à l’homme : « Tends la main. » L’homme l’a tendue, et sa main a été guérie. Elle était de nouveau normale.

decisions.choice: his hand was restored: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: his hand was restored, as healthy as the other, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "as healthy as the other", words found in Matthew 12:13. Early manuscripts lack them. The healing is complete either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: restored: brought back to its former healthy state
decisions.reason: The verb means to put back as it was.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whom Jesus spoke to.

source.text: αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας, καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: They then were filled with fury, and were discussing with one another what they might do to the Jesus.

en.L: But they were filled with senseless rage, and they were talking over with one another what they might do to Jesus.
en.B: This filled them with mindless rage, and they talked together about what they could do to Jesus.
en.R: But the teachers of the law and the Pharisees became wildly angry. They started talking with each other about what they could do to Jesus.

fr.L: Mais eux furent remplis d’une fureur insensée, et ils discutaient entre eux de ce qu’ils pourraient faire à Jésus.
fr.B: Ils en devinrent fous de rage, et ils se demandèrent ensemble ce qu’ils pourraient bien faire à Jésus.
fr.R: Mais les spécialistes de la Loi et les Pharisiens se sont mis dans une colère folle. Ils ont commencé à discuter entre eux de ce qu’ils pourraient faire contre Jésus.

decisions.choice: fury: rage that has lost all good sense
decisions.reason: The word means mindlessness. Here it is a fury so great that they cannot think clearly.

decisions.choice: what they might do: they are uncertain what to do
decisions.reason: The verb form expresses doubt. Luke does not yet speak of a plot to kill him, as Mark 3:6 does.

decisions.choice: the teachers of the law and the Pharisees
decisions.reason: Readable names who they were (6:7).

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι, καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: It came about then in the days these [that] to go out him to the mountain to pray, and he was spending the night in the prayer of the God.

en.L: And it happened in these days [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to the mountain to pray, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was spending the whole night in prayer to God.
en.B: During those days Jesus went off to the mountain to pray, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed up all night in prayer to God.
en.R: About that time, Jesus went up on a mountain to pray. He prayed to God all through the night.

fr.L: Or il arriva en ces jours-là qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit vers la montagne pour prier, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passait toute la nuit en prière à Dieu.
fr.B: En ces jours-là, Jésus s’en alla sur la montagne pour prier, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passa toute la nuit à prier Dieu.
fr.R: À cette époque, Jésus est monté sur une montagne pour prier. Il a prié Dieu toute la nuit.

decisions.choice: the prayer of God: prayer to God
alternatives: a place of prayer belonging to God
decisions.reason: The phrase names the one to whom the prayer is made.

decisions.choice: Jesus prays before the choice of the twelve
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus praying at the great moments of his work (3:21; 9:18, 28-29; 22:41-44). Here it comes before he chooses the twelve.

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hill country
decisions.reason: The article may point to the hills near the Sea of Galilee rather than a named mountain.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπ’ αὐτῶν δώδεκα, οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν, Σίμωνα ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριὼθ ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης.

records.literal_gloss: And when it became day, he called to [him] the disciples of him, and having chosen from them twelve, whom also apostles he named, \v 14 Simon whom also he named Peter, and Andrew the brother of him, and James and John and Philip and Bartholomew \v 15 and Matthew and Thomas and James [son] of Alphaeus and Simon the [one] called Zealot \v 16 and Judas [son] of James and Judas Iscariot, who became betrayer.

en.L: And when day came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to [{{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}], and choosing twelve from them, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also named apostles: \v 14 Simon, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John and Philip and Bartholomew \v 15 and Matthew and Thomas and James [son] of Alphaeus and Simon who was called [the] Zealot \v 16 and Judas [son] of James and Judas Iscariot, who became [a] betrayer.
en.B: At daybreak {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} summoned {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and picked out twelve of them, giving them the name apostles. \v 14 They were Simon, to whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the name Peter, and Simon's brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew; \v 15 Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus, and Simon, known as the Zealot; \v 16 Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, the one who turned traitor.
en.R: In the morning, Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. From them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose twelve men, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called them apostles, which means people who are sent out. \v 14 These were the twelve: Simon, whom Jesus also named Peter, and Simon's brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew; \v 15 Matthew and Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Simon, who was called the Zealot; \v 16 Judas, the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who later became a traitor.

fr.L: Et quand le jour vint, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appela {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples [auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], et, ayant choisi parmi eux douze, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nomma aussi apôtres : \v 14 Simon, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nomma aussi Pierre, et André son frère, et Jacques et Jean, et Philippe et Barthélemy, \v 15 et Matthieu et Thomas, et Jacques [fils] d’Alphée, et Simon appelé [le] Zélote, \v 16 et Judas [fils] de Jacques, et Judas Iscariot, qui devint traître.
fr.B: Au lever du jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appela {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et en choisit douze parmi eux, à qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna le nom d’apôtres. \v 14 C’étaient Simon, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nomma Pierre, et André, le frère de Simon ; Jacques et Jean ; Philippe et Barthélemy ; \v 15 Matthieu et Thomas ; Jacques, fils d’Alphée, et Simon, qu’on appelait le Zélote ; \v 16 Jude, fils de Jacques, et Judas Iscariot, celui qui devint un traître.
fr.R: Le matin, Jésus a appelé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples pour qu’ils viennent près de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Parmi eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisi douze hommes, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a appelés apôtres, un mot qui veut dire « envoyés ». \v 14 Voici ces douze hommes : Simon, que Jésus a aussi appelé Pierre, et André, le frère de Simon ; Jacques et Jean ; Philippe et Barthélemy ; \v 15 Matthieu et Thomas ; Jacques, le fils d’Alphée ; Simon, qu’on appelait le Zélote ; \v 16 Jude, le fils de Jacques ; et Judas Iscariot, qui plus tard est devenu un traître.

decisions.choice: apostles: men sent out as messengers, with the authority of the one who sends them
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to send out". Jesus will send the twelve out to preach and heal (9:1-2, 10). Luke often calls the twelve "the apostles" (17:5; 22:14; Acts 1:26).

decisions.choice: twelve: as many as the tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus gathers God's people anew around twelve leaders, as Israel had twelve tribes (22:30).

decisions.choice: Peter: a name meaning rock
decisions.reason: Jesus gave Simon the name. John 1:42 gives its Aramaic form, Cephas.

decisions.choice: the Zealot: either a man zealous for God's law, or one who had belonged to those who wanted to drive out Rome by force
alternatives: a member of the later Zealot party only
decisions.reason: The word means one full of zeal. The party called the Zealots took that name in the war against Rome in AD 66-70, but men of that kind were active before. Either way the name describes Simon's past or his character, and Jesus chose him with Matthew, who had collected taxes for Rome's rulers.

decisions.choice: Judas of James: Judas son of James
decisions.reason: The Greek gives only the name of a relative, which usually means the father. Jude 1 speaks of a Judas the brother of James, which led some to read "brother" here. Matthew 10:3 and Mark 3:18 have Thaddaeus in this place, probably another name for the same man.

decisions.choice: Iscariot: probably "man of Kerioth", a town in Judea
alternatives: a word meaning assassin or false one
decisions.reason: Kerioth is named in Joshua 15:25. Other explanations have been offered, and none is certain.

decisions.choice: betrayer: one who hands someone over to enemies
decisions.reason: Luke looks ahead to 22:3-6 and 22:47-48.

decisions.choice: the names set out in pairs, after "They were" (B) or "These were the twelve" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek list hangs on the first sentence. Balanced and Readable introduce it and group the names to make it easy to read.

decisions.choice: which means people who are sent out
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: the one who turned traitor (B); who later became a traitor (R)
decisions.reason: "Traitor" is the everyday word for one who betrays.

decisions.choice: Judas [fils] de Jacques (L); Jude, fils de Jacques (B, R); Judas Iscariot at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek gives both men the same name. Literal keeps it the same, so the reader sees it; Balanced and Readable follow the usual French custom of calling the first "Jude", which keeps him apart from Judas Iscariot.

decisions.choice: apôtres; douze in lowercase
decisions.reason: Here twelve is a number, not yet the title "les Douze" of the term sheet, so French writes it in lowercase, as Mark 3:14 does. Readable explains "apôtres" as the English Readable does (m1).

source.text: Καὶ καταβὰς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ, καὶ ὄχλος πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος, οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν· καὶ οἱ ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο·

records.literal_gloss: And having come down with them he stood on a place level, and a crowd large of disciples of him, and a multitude great of the people from all the Judea and Jerusalem and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon, \v 18 who came to hear him and to be healed from the diseases of them; and those troubled by spirits unclean were being healed;

en.L: And coming down with them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stood on a level place, and [there was] a large crowd of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, and a great multitude of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the coast of Tyre and Sidon, \v 18 who came to hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to be healed of their diseases; and those troubled by unclean spirits were being healed.
en.B: Coming down the mountain with them, Jesus stood on a flat stretch of ground. A big crowd of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples had gathered there, along with a huge number of people who had come from every part of Judea, from Jerusalem, and from the seacoast near Tyre and Sidon. \v 18 They came to listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to be cured of their illnesses, and people tormented by unclean spirits were made well.
en.R: Jesus came down from the mountain with the apostles and stood on a flat place. A large group of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples was there. A great crowd of other people was there too. They came from all over Judea, from Jerusalem, and from the towns by the sea near Tyre and Sidon. \v 18 They came to listen to Jesus and to be healed of their sicknesses. Some had evil spirits that troubled them, and Jesus made them well.

fr.L: Et, étant descendu avec eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se tint en un lieu plat, et [il y avait] une grande foule de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, et une grande multitude du peuple, de toute la Judée et de Jérusalem et du littoral de Tyr et de Sidon, \v 18 qui étaient venus pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendre et être guéris de leurs maladies ; et ceux qui étaient tourmentés par des esprits impurs étaient guéris.
fr.B: Jésus descendit de la montagne avec eux et s’arrêta sur un terrain plat. Une foule nombreuse de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples s’y trouvait, avec une très grande multitude de gens venus de toute la Judée, de Jérusalem et de la côte de Tyr et de Sidon. \v 18 Ils étaient venus pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écouter et pour être guéris de leurs maladies, et ceux que tourmentaient des esprits impurs recouvraient la santé.
fr.R: Jésus est descendu de la montagne avec les apôtres et il s’est arrêté dans un endroit plat. Un grand groupe de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples était là. Une foule d’autres gens était là aussi. Ils venaient de toute la Judée, de Jérusalem, et des villes au bord de la mer, près de Tyr et de Sidon. \v 18 Ils étaient venus pour écouter Jésus et pour être guéris de leurs maladies. Certains avaient des esprits mauvais qui les tourmentaient, et Jésus les a guéris.

decisions.choice: a level place: a flat area, perhaps a plateau among the hills
alternatives: the plain at the foot of the mountain
decisions.reason: Jesus comes down from the mountain where he prayed (6:12) to a place level enough for a crowd. Matthew sets similar teaching on the mountain (Matthew 5:1); a level place on a hillside fits both.

decisions.choice: a large crowd ... and a great multitude: these have no verb of their own
decisions.reason: The sense is that they were there with him.

decisions.choice: Judea: probably the whole land of the Jews
alternatives: only the southern region around Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Luke sometimes uses Judea for the whole Jewish land (1:5; 4:44; 7:17).

decisions.choice: the coast of Tyre and Sidon: the Gentile port cities to the north
decisions.reason: Tyre and Sidon lay on the Phoenician coast, outside the Jewish land (compare 4:26). People came even from there.

decisions.choice: unclean spirits: demons
decisions.reason: Luke uses "unclean spirit" and "demon" for the same beings (4:33). They are named apart from the diseases.

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: "Unclean" here means opposed to God's holiness, not dirty. Readable says "evil".

decisions.choice: down the mountain (B); from the mountain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where he came down from (6:12).

decisions.choice: Jesus made them well
decisions.reason: Readable names the healer; 6:19 makes clear that the power came from Jesus.

decisions.choice: des esprits impurs (L, B); des esprits mauvais (R)
alternatives: des esprits impurs at every level
decisions.reason: "Un esprit impur" is the term sheet's form for Literal and Balanced; Readable follows the English "evil spirits", as in Mark, since "impur" here does not mean dirty (m5).

source.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δύναμις παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας.

records.literal_gloss: And all the crowd were seeking to touch him, because power from him was going out and was healing all.

en.L: And all the crowd were seeking to touch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because power was going out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and healing [them] all.
en.B: Everyone in the crowd kept trying to touch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since power flowed out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and healed every one of them.
en.R: Everyone in the crowd tried to touch Jesus. Power was going out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and it healed all of them.

fr.L: Et toute la foule cherchait à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} toucher, parce qu’une puissance sortait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et les guérissait tous.
fr.B: Tout le monde dans la foule essayait de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} toucher, car une puissance émanait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et les guérissait tous, sans exception.
fr.R: Tout le monde dans la foule essayait de toucher Jésus. Une puissance sortait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et elle les guérissait tous.

decisions.choice: power: God's power at work through Jesus
alternatives: magic in his body or clothes
decisions.reason: The power of the Lord was with Jesus to heal (5:17). In 8:46 he feels power go out from him when a woman touches him in faith.

decisions.choice: were seeking ... was going out ... was healing: a scene that went on and on
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what kept happening all through that time.

source.text: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν· Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί, ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And he having lifted up the eyes of him to the disciples of him was saying, Blessed the poor, for yours is the kingdom of the God.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, lifting up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, was saying, "Blessed [are] the poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
en.B: Then, with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Blessed are you poor, for the kingdom of God is yours.
en.R: Jesus looked at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and said, "How blessed you are, you who are poor! The kingdom of God belongs to you.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, levant {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux vers {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, disait : « Heureux les pauvres, car c’est à vous qu’est le royaume de Dieu.
fr.B: Alors, les yeux fixés sur {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Heureux, vous les pauvres, car le royaume de Dieu vous appartient.
fr.R: Jésus a regardé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : « Vous êtes heureux, vous qui êtes pauvres ! Le royaume de Dieu est à vous.

decisions.choice: blessed: fortunate, in a happy state because of God's favor
alternatives: blessed by God, the word of 1:42
decisions.reason: The word is the one of 1:45. It declares people fortunate in God's eyes; it is neither a wish nor a command. "Happy" would sound like a passing feeling.

decisions.choice: the poor: people who are really poor, and who look to God for help
decisions.reason: Luke has no "in spirit" (compare Matthew 5:3). Jesus came to bring good news to the poor (4:18, from Isaiah 61:1). In the Psalms the poor are those who have no help but God (Psalm 34:7).

decisions.choice: the poor ... yours: Jesus speaks of the poor and to them in the same breath
decisions.reason: The saying begins in the third person and turns to "you". The disciples before him are among the poor he means (5:11, 28).

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: God's rule, already breaking in through Jesus and still to come in full
decisions.reason: Jesus announces the kingdom (4:43). It belongs now to the poor, as a promise and a present gift.

decisions.choice: you poor (B); you who are poor (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the turn to "you" from the start, so the saying reads as spoken to the disciples.

decisions.choice: How blessed you are
decisions.reason: Readable makes the declaration an exclamation, which is how it sounds.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 6:49, with a break only for the narrator's words at 6:39
decisions.reason: The sermon is one long speech.

decisions.choice: Heureux (L, B); Vous êtes heureux (R), for all four beatitudes (6:20-22)
decisions.reason: "Heureux" is the usual French word for the beatitudes and says the happy state of those God favours (m1); "bienheureux" now sounds churchly or suggests the blessed in heaven. Readable makes it a plain exclamation, as the English Readable does. "Le royaume de Dieu" is the term sheet's form.

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν, ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the hungering now, for you will be filled.

en.L: Blessed [are] those who hunger now, for you will be filled.
en.B: Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will eat your fill.
en.R: How blessed you are, you who are hungry now! God will give you plenty to eat.

fr.L: Heureux ceux qui ont faim maintenant, car vous serez rassasiés.
fr.B: Heureux, vous qui avez faim maintenant, car vous mangerez à votre faim.
fr.R: Vous êtes heureux, vous qui avez faim maintenant ! Dieu vous donnera beaucoup à manger.

decisions.choice: you will be filled: God will fill you
alternatives: you will find food for yourselves
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God unnamed, as Jewish speech often did. Mary sang that God fills the hungry with good things (1:53; Psalm 107:9).

decisions.choice: those who hunger now: people who really go hungry in this life
alternatives: those who hunger for righteousness only
decisions.reason: Luke has no "for righteousness" (compare Matthew 5:6). The word "now" sets their present need against God's coming reversal.

decisions.choice: God will give you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν, ὅτι γελάσετε.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the weeping now, for you will laugh.

en.L: Blessed [are] those who weep now, for you will laugh.
en.B: Blessed are those of you who are in tears now, for you will laugh.
en.R: How blessed you are, you who are crying now! The day will come when you laugh.

fr.L: Heureux ceux qui pleurent maintenant, car vous rirez.
fr.B: Heureux, vous qui êtes dans les larmes maintenant, car vous rirez.
fr.R: Vous êtes heureux, vous qui pleurez maintenant ! Un jour viendra où vous rirez.

decisions.choice: weep ... laugh: deep grief, and the joy of God's reversal
decisions.reason: Weeping is loud grief, as for the dead (8:52). Laughter here is the joy of people whose fortunes God has turned (Psalm 126:1-2).

decisions.choice: The day will come when
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the laughter lies ahead, as the future tense says.

source.text: Μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι, καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·

records.literal_gloss: Blessed are you when hate you the men, and when they exclude you and insult and cast out the name of you as evil on account of the Son of the Man;

en.L: Blessed are you when {{gender:people|men}} hate you, and when they exclude you and insult [you] and cast out your name as evil on account of the Son of Man.
en.B: Blessed are you when {{gender:people|men}} hate you and push you out of their company, when they insult you and throw out your name as something evil, all because of the Son of Man.
en.R: How blessed you are when {{gender:people|men}} hate you because of the Son of Man! They may shut you out and insult you. They may treat your very name as something evil.

fr.L: Heureux êtes-vous quand les {{gender:gens|hommes}} vous haïront, et quand ils vous excluront, et [vous] insulteront, et rejetteront votre nom comme mauvais, à cause du Fils de l’homme.
fr.B: Heureux êtes-vous quand les {{gender:gens|hommes}} vous haïront, quand ils vous tiendront à l’écart, qu’ils vous insulteront et rejetteront votre nom comme quelque chose de mauvais, à cause du Fils de l’homme.
fr.R: Vous êtes heureux quand les {{gender:gens|hommes}} vous détestent à cause du Fils de l’homme ! Il se peut qu’ils vous rejettent et qu’ils vous insultent. Ils traiteront peut-être votre nom même comme quelque chose de mauvais.

decisions.choice: exclude: separate, shut out from the community
decisions.reason: The verb means to mark off. It may include being put out of the synagogue (John 9:22; 16:2).

decisions.choice: cast out your name as evil: reject you as wicked, treating your name as a byword
alternatives: erase your name from a list
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person. It may also mean the name they bear as followers of Jesus (Acts 11:26; 1 Peter 4:14-16).

decisions.choice: on account of the Son of Man: because they belong to Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself by the title he uses in 6:5. His followers will suffer because they are his.

decisions.choice: push you out of their company (B); shut you out (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for being cut off from others.

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the ways they are mistreated, as possibilities
decisions.reason: Readable puts the cause up front and breaks the list into short sentences.

decisions.choice: les {{gender:gens|hommes}} for the plural of the word for human beings, in this sermon (6:22, 6:26, 6:31)
decisions.reason: The word means people in general. "Les gens" is the natural inclusive French for people at large; "les humains" would sound as if humanity were set against something else. The traditional "les hommes" is the alternative, as in English. The Greek subjunctive after "when" looks ahead, which French says with the future after "quand" (L, B).

source.text: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε, ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ· κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Rejoice in that the day and leap, look for the reward of you [is] great in the heaven; according to the same things for were doing to the prophets the fathers of them.

en.L: Rejoice in that day and leap [for joy], for look, your reward [is] great in heaven; for their fathers were doing the same things to the prophets.
en.B: Be glad when that day comes, and jump for joy, because a great reward is waiting for you in heaven. Their ancestors did the very same things to the prophets.
en.R: When that happens, be happy and jump for joy! God has a great reward for you in heaven. Long ago, their ancestors treated God's prophets in the same way.

fr.L: Réjouissez-vous en ce jour-là et bondissez [de joie], car voici, votre récompense [est] grande dans le ciel ; car c’est de la même manière que leurs pères agissaient envers les prophètes.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, réjouissez-vous et sautez de joie, car une grande récompense vous attend dans le ciel. C’est ainsi que leurs ancêtres ont traité les prophètes.
fr.R: Quand cela arrivera, soyez contents et sautez de joie ! Dieu vous réserve une grande récompense dans le ciel. Autrefois, leurs ancêtres ont traité les prophètes de Dieu de la même façon.

decisions.choice: your reward is great in heaven: God will reward you
decisions.reason: "In heaven" means with God, who keeps the reward for them. The reward is God's free gift, as 6:35 shows.

decisions.choice: their fathers: the ancestors of those who persecute
decisions.reason: Israel's prophets were often rejected and harmed (Jeremiah 20:1-2; 2 Chronicles 24:20-21; 11:47-51). Those who persecute Jesus's followers stand in that line.

decisions.choice: leap: jump for joy
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of John leaping in Elizabeth's womb (1:41, 44).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: God has a great reward for you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, who gives the reward.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The word means forefathers, not only fathers; "ancestors" says so, as at 1:55.

source.text: πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις, ὅτι ἀπέχετε τὴν παράκλησιν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: But woe to you the rich, for you are receiving in full the comfort of you.

en.L: But woe to you who are rich, for you are receiving your comfort in full.
en.B: But how terrible for you who are rich, because you already have your comfort in full.
en.R: But how terrible for you who are rich! You have already received all the comfort you are going to get.

fr.L: Mais malheur à vous, les riches, car vous recevez pleinement votre consolation.
fr.B: Mais malheur à vous, les riches : vous avez déjà toute votre consolation.
fr.R: Mais quel malheur pour vous qui êtes riches ! Vous avez déjà reçu tout le réconfort que vous allez recevoir.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning over people facing God's judgment
decisions.reason: The prophets used the cry (Isaiah 5:8-22; Amos 6:1). Each woe answers one of the blessings: the rich against the poor, the full against the hungry, the laughing against the weeping.

decisions.choice: you are receiving in full: you have had all you will get
alternatives: you are receiving some comfort now
decisions.reason: The verb was used on receipts: paid in full. Nothing more is owed.

decisions.choice: comfort: consolation
decisions.reason: The word is the one used of Israel's consolation in 2:25. Their wealth was all the comfort they looked for (compare 16:25).

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Woe" is rarely heard in everyday speech. Literal keeps the old cry; Balanced and Readable say what it means. All four woes (6:24-26) are worded the same way.

decisions.choice: malheur à vous (L, B); quel malheur pour vous (R), for all four woes (6:24-26)
alternatives: c’est terrible pour vous (B, R), as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form: French "malheur à vous" is still understood as a cry of grief and warning (m1), so Balanced keeps it where the English says "How terrible for you". Readable makes it a plain exclamation, as the English Readable does.

source.text: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι νῦν, ὅτι πεινάσετε.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, the having been filled now, for you will hunger.

en.L: Woe to you, the ones filled now, for you will hunger.
en.B: How terrible for you who have eaten your fill now, because you will know hunger.
en.R: How terrible for you who have more than enough to eat now! You will be hungry later.

fr.L: Malheur à vous qui êtes rassasiés maintenant, car vous aurez faim.
fr.B: Malheur à vous qui avez maintenant tout ce qu’il vous faut à manger, car vous connaîtrez la faim.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous qui avez maintenant plus qu’assez à manger ! Plus tard, vous aurez faim.

decisions.choice: who are full: who have eaten all they want
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a lasting state of being well fed. It answers the blessing on the hungry (6:21).

decisions.choice: the full will be hungry: God's reversal
decisions.reason: Mary sang that God sends the rich away empty (1:53).

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for all four woes (see 6:24).

source.text: οὐαί, οἱ γελῶντες νῦν, ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε.

records.literal_gloss: Woe, the laughing now, for you will mourn and weep.

en.L: Woe, the ones laughing now, for you will mourn and weep.
en.B: How terrible for you who are laughing now, because you will grieve and cry.
en.R: How terrible for you who are laughing now! You will be sad, and you will cry.

fr.L: Malheur, vous qui riez maintenant, car vous serez dans le deuil et vous pleurerez.
fr.B: Malheur à vous qui riez maintenant, car vous serez dans le deuil et dans les larmes.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous qui riez maintenant ! Vous serez tristes, et vous pleurerez.

decisions.choice: woe, with no "to you": the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: woe to you, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "to you" as in the first woe of the verse. The people spoken to are the same either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: mourn: grieve, as for the dead
decisions.reason: The laughter of the comfortable will turn to grief when God judges.

decisions.choice: Woe, the ones laughing (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for all four woes (see 6:24). Literal has no "to you", as the Greek has none.

source.text: Οὐαὶ ὅταν καλῶς ὑμᾶς εἴπωσιν πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι, κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Woe when well of you speak all the men, according to the same things for were doing to the false prophets the fathers of them.

en.L: Woe when all {{gender:people|men}} speak well of you, for their fathers were doing the same things to the false prophets.
en.B: How terrible for you when all {{gender:people|men}} praise you! Their ancestors did just the same for the false prophets.
en.R: How terrible for you when everyone says good things about you! Long ago, their ancestors spoke well of the false prophets in the same way.

fr.L: Malheur, quand tous les {{gender:gens|hommes}} disent du bien de vous, car c’est de la même manière que leurs pères agissaient envers les faux prophètes.
fr.B: Malheur à vous quand tous les {{gender:gens|hommes}} font votre éloge ! C’est ainsi que leurs ancêtres ont traité les faux prophètes.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous quand tout le monde dit du bien de vous ! Autrefois, leurs ancêtres ont dit du bien des faux prophètes de la même façon.

decisions.choice: woe, with no "to you": the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: woe to you, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "to you". The verb that follows is spoken to "you" in either reading. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: false prophets: people who claimed to speak for God but told people what they wanted to hear
decisions.reason: Jeremiah spoke of prophets who said "peace" when there was no peace, and the people loved it (Jeremiah 5:31; 6:14; 1 Kings 22:6-13).

decisions.choice: their fathers: the ancestors of those who now give praise
decisions.reason: As in 6:23, the ancestors of the speakers. Being praised by everyone may mean saying only what pleases.

decisions.choice: How terrible for you
decisions.reason: The same wording for all four woes (see 6:24); "you" is clear from the verb that follows.

decisions.choice: says good things about you (R); praise you (B)
decisions.reason: Plain words for the same thing.

source.text: Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν λέγω τοῖς ἀκούουσιν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς, εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμᾶς, προσεύχεσθε περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: But to you I say, to those hearing, love the enemies of you, well do to those hating you, \v 28 bless those cursing you, pray concerning those mistreating you.

en.L: But I say to you, the ones hearing: love your enemies; treat well those hating you; \v 28 bless those cursing you; pray for those mistreating you.
en.B: But to you who are listening I say this: love your enemies. Treat those who hate you well. \v 28 Speak blessings on those who curse you, and pray for those who treat you badly.
en.R: But I am telling you who are listening to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: Love your enemies. Be good to people who hate you. \v 28 Ask God to bless people who curse you. Pray for people who are cruel to you.

fr.L: Mais à vous qui entendez, je dis : aimez vos ennemis ; traitez bien ceux qui vous haïssent ; \v 28 bénissez ceux qui vous maudissent ; priez pour ceux qui vous outragent.
fr.B: Mais à vous qui écoutez, je dis ceci : aimez vos ennemis. Montrez-vous bons envers ceux qui vous détestent. \v 28 Prononcez des bénédictions sur ceux qui vous maudissent, et priez pour ceux qui vous traitent mal.
fr.R: Mais je vous le dis, à vous qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écoutez : aimez vos ennemis. Soyez bons avec ceux qui vous détestent. \v 28 Demandez à Dieu de bénir ceux qui vous maudissent. Priez pour ceux qui sont méchants avec vous.

decisions.choice: but to you who hear: Jesus turns from the woes to those listening
alternatives: a contrast with the law of Moses
decisions.reason: "But" marks the turn from the people under the woes to those who hear and will obey (6:47).

decisions.choice: love: active goodwill shown in deeds
decisions.reason: The commands that follow show what this love does: it treats well, blesses and prays. Leviticus 19:18 commanded love for one's neighbor; Jesus extends it to enemies.

decisions.choice: bless those who curse you: ask God's good for those who call down harm on you
decisions.reason: To curse was to call on God to bring harm; to bless was to call on him to give good (Romans 12:14).

decisions.choice: mistreat: insult, abuse, threaten
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat someone spitefully (1 Peter 3:16).

decisions.choice: speak blessings on
decisions.reason: Balanced makes clear that blessing is spoken, as cursing is.

decisions.choice: Ask God to bless
decisions.reason: Readable says what blessing someone means, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: τῷ τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα μὴ κωλύσῃς.

records.literal_gloss: To the one striking you on the cheek offer also the other, and from the one taking away of you the cloak also the tunic do not withhold.

en.L: To the one striking you on the cheek, hold out the other [one] also, and from the one taking away your cloak, do not keep back the tunic also.
en.B: If anyone strikes you on the cheek, present the other one as well. If anyone takes your coat, let {{gender:them|him}} have your shirt too.
en.R: If someone hits you on one side of your face, let {{gender:them|him}} hit the other side too. If someone takes your coat, do not stop {{gender:them|him}} from taking your shirt as well.

fr.L: À celui qui te frappe sur la joue, présente aussi l’autre, et à celui qui t’enlève ton manteau, ne refuse pas non plus la tunique.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un te frappe sur la joue, tends-lui aussi l’autre. Si quelqu’un te prend ton manteau, abandonne-lui aussi ta chemise.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un te frappe sur une joue, laisse-le te frapper aussi sur l’autre. Si quelqu’un te prend ton manteau, laisse-le aussi prendre ta chemise.

decisions.choice: striking on the cheek: an insult as much as an injury
decisions.reason: A slap on the face was a public insult (Lamentations 3:30; Isaiah 50:6). Jesus speaks of not striking back, not of failing to protect others.

decisions.choice: cloak and tunic: the outer garment and the inner one worn next to the skin
decisions.reason: In Luke the cloak is taken first, which suggests a robbery; Matthew 5:40 speaks of a lawsuit. The tunic was the last garment a person had (3:11).

decisions.choice: do not hold back: do not refuse
alternatives: do not take back by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to hinder or keep from.

decisions.choice: coat ... shirt
decisions.reason: The nearest everyday words for the outer and inner garments, as at 3:11.

decisions.choice: "tu" for these sayings; "quelqu’un … lui, le" with no gender setting, for the whole sermon (6:29, 6:40, 6:47-49)
alternatives: vous, as in the surrounding verses
a gender span on the pronouns, as the English has
decisions.reason: The Greek turns to the singular in 6:29-30, so French says "tu", as the style guide asks. Where the English needs a gender span for a pronoun, French "quelqu’un", "celui qui" and the "lui", "le" and "il" that refer back to them already mean anyone, so no span is added (style guide, section 7).

source.text: παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει.

records.literal_gloss: To everyone asking you give, and from the one taking away the yours not ask back.

en.L: To everyone asking you, give; and from the one taking away what [is] yours, do not demand [it] back.
en.B: Keep giving to everyone who asks you for something, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not ask for it back.
en.R: Whenever someone asks you for something, give it. If someone takes things that belong to you, do not ask for them back.

fr.L: À quiconque te demande, donne ; et à celui qui t’enlève ce qui est à toi, ne [le] réclame pas.
fr.B: Donne toujours à quiconque te demande quelque chose, et si quelqu’un prend ce qui t’appartient, ne le lui réclame pas.
fr.R: Chaque fois que quelqu’un te demande quelque chose, donne-le-lui. Si quelqu’un te prend des choses qui sont à toi, ne les lui redemande pas.

decisions.choice: give ... do not demand back: present tense, what one does again and again
decisions.reason: The commands describe a way of living, not a single gift.

decisions.choice: demand back: reclaim what was taken
alternatives: ask for a loan to be repaid
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask back what is one's own.

decisions.choice: Keep giving
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the force of the present tense, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως.

records.literal_gloss: And as you want that should do to you the men, do to them likewise.

en.L: And just as you want {{gender:people|men}} to do to you, do to them likewise.
en.B: However you want {{gender:people|men}} to treat you, treat them the same way.
en.R: Think about how you want others to treat you. Then treat them that way.

fr.L: Et selon que vous voulez que les {{gender:gens|hommes}} agissent envers vous, agissez pareillement envers eux.
fr.B: La manière dont vous voulez que les {{gender:gens|hommes}} vous traitent, traitez-les de la même façon.
fr.R: Pensez à la manière dont vous voulez que les autres vous traitent. Puis traitez-les de cette manière.

decisions.choice: treat others as you want to be treated: a positive command
alternatives: only a warning not to harm
decisions.reason: Jewish teaching knew the saying in a negative form: do to no one what you hate (Tobit 4:15). Jesus states it as a command to act. Matthew 7:12 adds that this sums up the Law and the Prophets.

decisions.choice: two sentences: think, then treat
decisions.reason: Readable splits the saying into two short steps.

source.text: Καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν;

records.literal_gloss: And if you love those loving you, what kind of to you credit is it?

en.L: And if you love those loving you, what kind of credit is [it] to you?
en.B: If you love those who love you, what thanks do you deserve?
en.R: If you love only the people who love you, should anyone thank you for that?

fr.L: Et si vous aimez ceux qui vous aiment, quelle reconnaissance vous [en] revient ?
fr.B: Si vous aimez ceux qui vous aiment, quelle reconnaissance méritez-vous ?
fr.R: Si vous aimez seulement les gens qui vous aiment, est-ce qu’on doit vous dire merci pour cela ?

decisions.choice: credit: thanks, the favor earned by an act that deserves it
decisions.reason: The word usually translated "grace" here means credit or thanks. The question asks what is so special about such love. Matthew 5:46 has "what reward"; some read the thanks as God's favor (compare 6:35).

decisions.choice: what kind of: a question expecting the answer none
alternatives: a real question about how much credit
decisions.reason: The question says that such love deserves no special thanks.

decisions.choice: credit (L); thanks (B); thank you (R)
decisions.reason: The key term "grace" would mislead here, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast clear: love that goes only to those who love back.

decisions.choice: quelle reconnaissance (L, B); est-ce qu’on doit vous dire merci (R), in 6:32-34
decisions.reason: As in English, the key term "grâce" would mislead here (m1): the word means the thanks an act deserves. "Quel mérite" would bring in the idea of earning merit before God. "Reconnaissance" is the gratitude owed.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Even for the sinners those loving them love.

en.L: For even the sinners love those loving them.
en.B: After all, sinners too love those who love them back.
en.R: Even sinful people love those who love them.

fr.L: Car même les pécheurs aiment ceux qui les aiment.
fr.B: Après tout, les pécheurs aussi aiment ceux qui les aiment en retour.
fr.R: Même ceux qui désobéissent à Dieu aiment les gens qui les aiment.

decisions.choice: sinners: people known for not keeping God's law
decisions.reason: In the Gospels "sinners" are people who openly ignore God's law, often named with tax collectors (5:30). Matthew 5:46 has "tax collectors" here.

decisions.choice: sinful people
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase.

decisions.choice: les pécheurs (L, B); ceux qui désobéissent à Dieu (R), in 6:32-34
decisions.reason: "Les pécheurs" is the term sheet's word. The English Readable uses a plain phrase; French Readable does the same and says what made them sinners (m1).

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν;

records.literal_gloss: And if you do good to those doing good to you, what kind of to you credit is it?

en.L: And if you do good to those doing good to you, what kind of credit is [it] to you?
en.B: And if you do good to those who do good to you, what thanks do you deserve?
en.R: If you do good things only for people who do good things for you, should anyone thank you for that?

fr.L: Et si vous faites du bien à ceux qui vous font du bien, quelle reconnaissance vous [en] revient ?
fr.B: Et si vous faites du bien à ceux qui vous en font, quelle reconnaissance méritez-vous ?
fr.R: Si vous faites du bien seulement aux gens qui vous font du bien, est-ce qu’on doit vous dire merci pour cela ?

decisions.choice: credit: thanks, the favor earned by an act that deserves it
decisions.reason: As in 6:32, the word usually translated "grace" means credit or thanks.

decisions.choice: credit (L); thanks (B); thank you (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:32.

source.text: καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Even the sinners the same do.

en.L: Even the sinners do the same.
en.B: Even sinners do as much.
en.R: Sinful people do that too.

fr.L: Même les pécheurs font la même chose.
fr.B: Les pécheurs en font autant.
fr.R: Ceux qui désobéissent à Dieu le font aussi.

decisions.choice: even: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: for even, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "for", as in 6:32. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν δανίσητε παρ’ ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν;

records.literal_gloss: And if you lend [to those] from whom you hope to receive, what kind of to you credit is it?

en.L: And if you lend [to those] from whom you hope to receive [back], what kind of credit is [it] to you?
en.B: And if you lend to people you expect to pay you back, what thanks do you deserve?
en.R: If you lend money only to people who you think will pay you back, should anyone thank you for that?

fr.L: Et si vous prêtez [à ceux] de qui vous espérez recevoir [en retour], quelle reconnaissance vous [en] revient ?
fr.B: Et si vous prêtez à ceux dont vous attendez d’être remboursés, quelle reconnaissance méritez-vous ?
fr.R: Si vous prêtez de l’argent seulement à ceux qui, pensez-vous, vous rembourseront, est-ce qu’on doit vous dire merci pour cela ?

decisions.choice: credit: thanks, the favor earned by an act that deserves it
decisions.reason: As in 6:32, the word usually translated "grace" means credit or thanks.

decisions.choice: lend: lending to a neighbor in need
decisions.reason: The law told Israel to lend freely to a poor neighbor and not to charge interest (Deuteronomy 15:7-8; Leviticus 25:35-37).

decisions.choice: credit (L); thanks (B); thank you (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:32.

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Readable says what is lent.

source.text: καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς δανίζουσιν ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα.

records.literal_gloss: Even sinners to sinners lend so that they might receive back the equal [things].

en.L: Even sinners lend to sinners so that they may receive back the same [amount].
en.B: Sinners also lend to sinners, so as to get back as much again.
en.R: Even sinful people lend to other sinful people, so that they will get back the same amount.

fr.L: Même des pécheurs prêtent à des pécheurs afin de recevoir en retour autant.
fr.B: Les pécheurs aussi prêtent aux pécheurs, pour qu’on leur rende autant.
fr.R: Même ceux qui désobéissent à Dieu prêtent à d’autres comme eux, pour qu’on leur rende la même somme.

decisions.choice: the same: the same amount as was lent
alternatives: a like favor in return, a loan when they need one
decisions.reason: The words mean "the equal things". Either way, the lender looks for a return.

source.text: πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε μηδὲν ἀπελπίζοντες· καὶ ἔσται ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολύς, καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου, ὅτι αὐτὸς χρηστός ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς.

records.literal_gloss: But love the enemies of you and do good and lend nothing expecting in return; and will be the reward of you great, and you will be sons of [the] Most High, for he kind is to the ungrateful and evil.

en.L: Rather, love your enemies and do good and lend, hoping for nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be {{gender:children|sons}} of [the] Most High, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is kind toward the ungrateful and evil [ones].
en.B: Instead, love your enemies, treat them well, and lend without hoping to get anything back. Then you will receive a great reward, and you will be {{gender:children|sons}} of the Most High, since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good to the thankless and the wicked.
en.R: Instead, love your enemies. Do good to them. Lend to them, and do not expect to get anything back. Then you will have a great reward, and you will be {{gender:children|sons}} of God Most High. For God is kind to people who never thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to people who are evil.

fr.L: Au contraire, aimez vos ennemis, et faites du bien, et prêtez sans rien espérer en retour ; et votre récompense sera grande, et vous serez {{gender:enfants|fils}} du Très-Haut, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est bon envers les ingrats et les méchants.
fr.B: Aimez plutôt vos ennemis, faites-leur du bien, et prêtez sans espérer qu’on vous rende quoi que ce soit. Alors vous recevrez une grande récompense, et vous serez {{gender:enfants|fils}} du Très-Haut, puisqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est bon pour les ingrats et pour les méchants.
fr.R: Au contraire, aimez vos ennemis. Faites-leur du bien. Prêtez-leur, et n’attendez pas qu’on vous rende quelque chose. Alors vous aurez une grande récompense, et vous serez {{gender:enfants|fils}} du Dieu Très-Haut. Car Dieu est bon avec ceux qui ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent jamais merci, et avec ceux qui sont méchants.

decisions.choice: hoping for nothing back: expecting no return
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to give up hope. Here, after "lend" and set against 6:34, it means to hope for something in return.

decisions.choice: nothing: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: no one, the reading of a few early manuscripts, giving "despairing of no one"
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts have a form meaning "no one", which gives the sense "giving up on no one". Most have "nothing". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: children of the Most High: people who share God's character
alternatives: a title earned by good works
decisions.reason: Children take after their father. Those who love their enemies act as God acts. "The Most High" is a name for God (1:32, 35; Genesis 14:18-20). The word is "sons", but the saying is for all who listen.

decisions.choice: kind: good, generous
decisions.reason: The word describes goodness that gives to those who do not deserve it.

decisions.choice: rather: a strong contrast with 6:32-34
decisions.reason: Jesus sets his command against the way sinners love, do good and lend.

decisions.choice: treat them well (B); Do good to them (R)
decisions.reason: The context shows that the enemies are the ones to whom good is done.

decisions.choice: God Most High
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "the Most High" is God, as at 1:35.

source.text: γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες καθὼς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν οἰκτίρμων ἐστίν·

records.literal_gloss: Become compassionate as the Father of you compassionate is.

en.L: Become compassionate, as your Father is compassionate.
en.B: Show compassion, as your Father shows compassion.
en.R: Have compassion for others, just as your Father has compassion.

fr.L: Devenez compatissants, comme votre Père est compatissant.
fr.B: Faites preuve de compassion, comme votre Père fait preuve de compassion.
fr.R: Ayez de la compassion pour les autres, comme votre Père a de la compassion.

decisions.choice: compassionate: feeling pity and acting on it
decisions.reason: The word is not the usual one for mercy. It is used of God in the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 34:6 and Psalm 103:8 (102:8 in that numbering): the LORD is compassionate and gracious.

decisions.choice: become: a call to grow into this likeness
alternatives: be, as a state already reached
decisions.reason: The verb means to become; the present tense shows a way of life.

decisions.choice: your Father: God, the Father of those who belong to him
decisions.reason: This picks up "children of the Most High" in 6:35.

decisions.choice: compassionate (L); show compassion (B); have compassion (R)
decisions.reason: The usual word is "merciful", but the Greek word stresses pity that moves to help.

source.text: Καὶ μὴ κρίνετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε· καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: And not judge, and not not you will be judged; and not condemn, and not not you will be condemned.

en.L: And do not judge, and you will certainly not be judged; and do not condemn, and you will certainly not be condemned.
en.B: Do not sit in judgment on others, and you will never be judged. Do not pass sentence on them, and no sentence will be passed on you.
en.R: Do not judge other people, and God will not judge you. Do not say that others are guilty, and God will not say that you are guilty.

fr.L: Et ne jugez pas, et vous ne serez en aucun cas jugés ; et ne condamnez pas, et vous ne serez en aucun cas condamnés.
fr.B: Ne vous faites pas les juges des autres, et vous ne serez jamais jugés. Ne prononcez pas de condamnation contre eux, et aucune condamnation ne sera prononcée contre vous.
fr.R: Ne jugez pas les autres, et Dieu ne vous jugera pas. Ne dites pas que les autres sont coupables, et Dieu ne dira pas que vous êtes coupables.

decisions.choice: judge: pass judgment on others, find fault
decisions.reason: Jesus forbids setting oneself up as judge over others. He still asks his hearers to tell good fruit from bad (6:43-45).

decisions.choice: you will certainly not be judged: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together for emphasis.

decisions.choice: be judged, be condemned: by God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God unnamed, as in 6:21 and 6:38.

decisions.choice: sit in judgment ... pass sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the picture of a judge in court.

decisions.choice: God will not judge you ... God will not say
alternatives: you will not be judged ... condemned
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decision explains.
